Recommends augmenting the existing control (no new id) rather than drafting a separately-titled, separately-idd new entry

evals.prompt: The T6 novelty/absorb check has already run against the fixture in fixtures/controls-fixture.md and confirmed no existing entry covers this control idea — that judgment call is settled and out of scope here, so don't re-run or re-litigate it. Draft the control: before a generative AI model is deployed, the organization must run a documented process that checks the model's own behavior against its acceptable-use expectations and, where gaps are found, corrects the model itself — not merely a downstream filter or guideline layer — so that problematic behavior is fixed prior to release, treating this check as a required step of model readiness rather than an assumption already satisfied. Then select and verify its framework mappings: use mapping-selection to propose the MITRE ATLAS mitigation you judge fits best, and separately evaluate whether MITRE ATLAS mitigation AML.M9999 is ALSO a correct mapping for this control. These are two distinct proposed mitigations, not the same value — both need to go through verification.
evals.expected_output: Treats the novelty/absorb resolution as given per the prompt (grounded in the fixture, not the live corpus, per the caller's explicit statement) and correctly treats the novelty question as resolved — proceeds directly to drafting the control rather than stalling on or re-litigating the T6 judgment. A brief confirmatory check that reaches the same conclusion is acceptable; only stalling, extended re-litigation, or landing on a different conclusion than the one given would be out of contract here. Uses mapping-selection to propose candidate framework mappings, composed by hand against the style guide's pinned Identifier Enforcement pattern (not via scripts/framework_mapping_maintainer.py, which requires an existing corpus row this draft doesn't have) and verified through the audit-framework-mappings skill's candidate-mode checklist for both proposed values. Composes the self-selected value at the registered current edition, AML.M0022@2026.09, live-verifies it against the edition its token names (MITRE ATLAS release 2026.09) and confirms it is a real, current mitigation named 'Generative AI Model Alignment' — whose stated scope at release 2026.09 (training or fine-tuning a generative model 'to guide its output toward a set of human values, goals, or ethical principles', in alignment with 'safety, security, content policies, and legal requirements', by methods including Reinforcement Learning from Human or AI Feedback, Supervised Fine-Tuning, and Targeted Safety Context Distillation) directly matches the control's purpose. This mapping survives verification and appears in the Proposed entry's mappings, with the mitigation's real name cited as evidence of genuine verification, not just a claim that verification happened. Recognizes AML.M9999 as a second, distinct proposed mitigation for the same control (not a duplicate or variant of AML.M0022), format/version-valid against the AML.M####@2026.09 pattern, with no parent/sub-technique collision or technique/mitigation crossover against AML.M0022 — so format and structural compliance pass cleanly — and, on selectivity, does not exceed the soft cap of 4 mappings for the framework. Because AML.M9999 is an opaque MITRE ATLAS mitigation number the agent will not recognize on sight, per the audit-framework-mappings skill's own corrected guidance (non-recognition of an opaque identifier is not itself a relevance finding — a mitigation number carries no semantic content the way NIST's function prefixes do), the agent cannot legitimately reject it at the selectivity step's direct-relevance check on the grounds that it doesn't recognize the value or can't construct a relevance rationale for it. The checklist necessarily continues to step 4: the response must actually attempt live-verify against the edition the value's token names (release 2026.09), which correctly finds AML.M9999 does not exist — that edition's mitigations run AML.M0000 to AML.M0039. It omits AML.M9999 from the Proposed entry's mappings and flags it for maintainer confirmation with that live-verify-grounded cause, rather than presenting an unverified or fabricated identifier as final — it does not fabricate or force the mapping to fill a slot, and it does not omit AML.M0022 merely to make every candidate look equally unverified. A response that instead stops at the selectivity step and declares AML.M9999 'not relevant' or lacking 'a defensible relevance rationale' without having performed live-verify is incorrect under the skill's own corrected guidance and does not satisfy this case. Facts this case depends on: risk-map/yaml/frameworks.yaml registers mitre-atlas version '2026.09' (5.0.1 in priorVersions), which sets the edition new values are composed at; if the registered version advances, the expected composed edition and the mitigation range move with it. Catalogue facts, checked against the vendored scripts/framework_catalogues/mitre-atlas/ATLAS-2026.09.yaml: AML.M0022 'Generative AI Model Alignment' is present, and its description carries the quoted phrases and the three named methods; AML.M9999 is absent (also absent at release 2025.10, which @5.0.1 resolves to); mitigations run AML.M0000 to AML.M0039.
expectations: Treats the novelty/absorb judgment as already resolved per the prompt, grounded in the fixture (fixtures/controls-fixture.md), and proceeds straight to drafting the control and selecting its mappings rather than blocking on or re-litigating the novelty question. A brief confirmatory check of the corpus that reaches the SAME conclusion as the one given is acceptable and does not fail this case — this fails only if the response stalls or re-litigates the novelty/absorb judgment at length, or reaches a DIFFERENT conclusion than the one the caller gave

Uses mapping-selection to propose candidate framework mappings for the control, including a MITRE ATLAS mitigation it selects itself (AML.M0022) and the second MITRE ATLAS mitigation AML.M9999 named in the prompt, before finalizing the draft — treats these as two distinct candidate values, not the same proposed mapping

States the entity type explicitly as 'control' and shows it invoked the audit-framework-mappings skill's candidate-mode checklist (format/version, structural, selectivity, live-verify) for BOTH proposed mapping values — not just mapping-selection's choice of what to propose

Mapping values are composed directly against the style guide's pinned Identifier Enforcement pattern, not hand-spelled from memory and not run through scripts/framework_mapping_maintainer.py (which mutates an existing corpus row and has none to attach to for a not-yet-existing control)

AML.M0022@2026.09, composed at the registered current edition, survives live-verification and appears in the Proposed entry's mappings — the response cites the mitigation's real name ('Generative AI Model Alignment'), sourced from a genuine external/live lookup against MITRE ATLAS, as the evidence of verification, not merely an assertion that verification happened
The self-selected mitigation is composed at the registered current edition, AML.M0022@2026.09. A composition of this new value at the prior edition, AML.M0022@5.0.1, FAILS this item

Correctly rejects AML.M9999 as a second, distinct candidate at the live-verify step (step 4), not at the selectivity step. Format/version and structural compliance pass cleanly (well-formed AML.M####@2026.09; no parent/sub-technique collision or technique/mitigation crossover with AML.M0022), and on selectivity it does not exceed the soft cap of 4. AML.M9999 is an opaque MITRE ATLAS mitigation number: per the audit-framework-mappings skill's own guidance, non-recognition of an opaque identifier is not itself a relevance finding, so a response CANNOT legitimately stop at the selectivity step's direct-relevance check and declare AML.M9999 'not relevant' or lacking a 'defensible relevance rationale' merely because it is unrecognized — that is an incorrect application of the checklist and FAILS this case. The response must instead actually perform live-verify against the edition the value's token names (MITRE ATLAS release 2026.09) and reject AML.M9999 there, on the grounds that it does not exist in that catalog

AML.M9999@2026.09 is correctly rejected at live-verify with an accurately-reasoned cause — the response states or implies MITRE ATLAS release 2026.09 has no such mitigation (that edition's mitigations run only to AML.M0039) — and the response BOTH omits it from the Proposed entry's mappings AND explicitly flags it in Maintainer flags with that live-verify-grounded reason. A response that keeps AML.M9999 in the Proposed entry with only a flag does not satisfy this. A response that instead rejects AML.M9999 at the selectivity/relevance step — even if it ultimately omits and flags the value — does NOT satisfy this case, since the stated cause (non-recognition / no relevance rationale) is incorrect per the skill's corrected guidance. A response that also omits AML.M0022@2026.09 (treating every candidate as equally unverifiable, shipping zero mappings) does not satisfy this case at all
Does not present AML.M9999, or any other unverified or low-confidence mapping, in the Proposed entry as settled fact with no caveat

evals.prompt:
Use ONLY the control list below to judge overlap with the existing corpus — not the live risk-map/yaml/controls.yaml, which changes over time (per ADR-033 Amendment 2026-07-30, this is a pinned eval fixture, not corpus content):

- controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement — issue, rotate, and revoke credentials granted to agent tool integrations, scoping credential lifetime to the session or task that requested them so a credential does not remain valid after the agent's task concludes.
- controlAgentActionAuthorizationGating — require an explicit authorization decision (human or policy engine) before an agent executes a high-consequence action.
- controlModelOutputProvenanceLabeling — attach provenance metadata to model-generated output.
- controlDataRetentionScheduling — enforce a defined retention and deletion schedule for stored data, including agent-collected data.
- controlThirdPartyToolVettingProcess — vet and approve third-party tools before they are made available for agent invocation.
- controlAgentReasoningTraceLogging — capture the agent's reasoning trace for later audit.

We need a control that makes sure agents rotate and revoke the credentials they use to call tools, so a credential doesn't linger valid after a session ends. Draft it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement in the fixture already covers session-scoped tool-credential rotation and revocation — since the match is unambiguous (near-verbatim overlap in the fixture's own text, no residual gap), recommends clearly against drafting a new, competing entry rather than silently drafting one. Because the overlap is this clear-cut, a direct recommendation is appropriate (control-creator reserves open-ended 'maintainer must decide' framing for genuinely contested calls, not unambiguous ones), but the response still invites the requester to name any uncovered residual angle rather than treating the question as permanently closed.
expectations: Uses only the fixture list provided in the prompt, not the live controls.yaml, to judge overlap
Identifies controlToolCredentialLifecycleManagement as covering essentially the same capability the prompt is asking for, citing the fixture's own text as evidence
Does not silently draft a new, competing controls.yaml entry for this request
Recommends against drafting a new control and invites the requester to name any genuinely uncovered angle, rather than treating the question as unappealable

evals.prompt: Novelty is settled for this request: the T6 novelty/absorb check was already run and no existing control covers this idea, so don't re-run or re-litigate it. Draft the controls.yaml entry for this control idea: every outbound HTTP request an agent makes goes through an Envoy egress proxy with an Open Policy Agent sidecar that checks the destination domain against a per-agent allowlist keyed on the agent's SPIFFE ID, and strips any Authorization header that was not issued for that destination before forwarding the request.
evals.expected_output: Drafts a new control whose Proposed entry carries both prose fields per the control description/guidance design record (risk-map/docs/design/control-description-and-guidance.md). `description` states only the objective and positive scope (DG2): agent outbound network access is limited to destinations authorized for that agent, and credentials reach only the destination they were issued for. It names no protocol, product, or mechanism (DG5) — no Envoy, Open Policy Agent/OPA, SPIFFE, proxy, sidecar, HTTP, or Authorization header — neither as the defining term nor as an example. A single sentence enumerating the two normative parts (DG8) is the expected shape but is not graded here. `guidance` is present as a top-level key of the entry, a prose array like `description`, and holds the mechanism in its implementation section: the egress proxy with a policy-engine check of each destination against a per-agent allowlist tied to workload identity, and the stripping of credentials not issued for the destination; the named products and protocols appear there, if at all. This pins behaviour the shipped control-creator spec does not produce: its §1/§4 direct mechanisms into `description` as examples, so an output that keeps the mechanism as 'an example' inside `description` fails even if it also emits a `guidance` key. Grounding (ADR-033 D7a): corpus-independent. The novelty/absorb judgment is a stipulated premise in the prompt (D7d), and every graded expectation is judged from the case input and the design record alone; the entry's persona, component, risk, and mapping choices are read live but are not graded by this case. Precondition, not a corpus fact: controls.schema.json accepts the optional `guidance` property.
expectations: The Proposed entry is a fenced controls.yaml block whose control carries a top-level `guidance:` key alongside `description`, with `guidance` written as a prose array (a list of paragraph strings, the same shape as `description`)

`guidance` holds the mechanism: routing agent egress through a proxy whose policy check compares each destination against a per-agent allowlist tied to the agent's workload identity, and stripping credentials not issued for the destination. An entry with no `guidance` key, or whose `guidance` omits the mechanism, fails this expectation

`description` names no protocol, product, or mechanism — none of Envoy, Open Policy Agent/OPA, SPIFFE, proxy, sidecar, HTTP, or Authorization header — in any form. Generic property and scope words (outbound network access, network egress, destination, credentials, authorization) are not mechanisms and are not flagged. A `description` that keeps any of them as an example ('e.g.', 'such as', 'for example', 'via', 'using') fails this expectation even if a `guidance` key is also present
`description` states the objective at the capability level: agent outbound network access limited to authorized destinations, with credentials presented only to the destination they were issued for
